identity: Arabic literary translation of Dickens's ghost story 'The Signal-Man' (عامل التحويلة). Title line, then first-person Victorian narrative with a few shouted one-line utterances set off as their own paragraphs. Register = my doctrine's SS-N/SS-O: translated literary narrative, long periodic sentences, heavy subordination, chains of و/ف/حتى-clauses inside a single printed sentence.
law: The unit is the translator's printed full stop, nothing else. Units run 15-35 tokens. Every <NL> is free (13 of them here, incl. the title and the two shouted lines). Inside paragraphs I cut ONLY where the English/Arabic period falls: at the end of a completed narrative proposition. و / ف / حتى إن / بينما / كما لو / حيث / ولكن are continuation markers and weld (LAW 1, LAW 2, B4). Semicolon-joined correlatives ('so little sunlight ... that; and so much cold wind ... that') stay welded because the translator carried them with و.
reasoning: @47-48 'ولكن بدلا من أن ينظر': the English has a semicolon before 'but', but B4 is emphatic that ولكن welds at any length unless a real end-stop precedes; welded, cutting instead at 74 where the period actually lands. @122 'أما أنا فكنت فوقه' looks like a fresh topic with a new subject but it is the second half of the 'his figure was foreshortened ... and mine was high above him, so steeped in the glow ... that I had shaded my eyes' period - welded, boundary deferred to the free <NL> at 139. @264 'كررت سؤالي' is only two tokens and is followed by و, which by LAW 1 argues weld; I cut anyway because Dickens prints 'I repeated my inquiry.' as its own sentence and Hindawi translations preserve sentence-level stops - flagged lo. @297-298 'قائلا حسنا واتجهت': H3 says a bare interjection is its own segment, but that rule is scoped to balloons and conversational turns; here «حسنا» sits mid-sentence between a speech verb and a following و-clause, so G1 (quote welds to its speech verb) governs - welded. @472-522 is a 51-token period built of ف...و...و rendering three English semicolon clauses; LAW 2 says ف and ثم count AGAINST cutting, so one segment. @541 'وكان قدر كبير من الرياح' is the second limb of a 'so...that / and so...that' correlative - welded to 559. @605 'وهو ما لفت انتباهي' is a trailing relative adjunct (LAW 4) and stays with its main clause.
